question: Which intuitionistic proofs can be transported to the classical extension, and why can the reverse identity-on-formulas interpretation not preserve all proofs?
scope: One common propositional language with two distinct inductive derivability relations, a proof-preserving interpretation interface, composition, and a Kripke obstruction to the reverse identity translation. Not a cross-kernel, ZF, or arbitrary nonidentity translation theorem.

variants.statement: IPC Γ φ → CPC Γ φ
variants.construction: Direct induction transporting every intuitionistic derivation constructor

variants.statement: Interpretation IPC CPC transports derivations and contexts
IPC → CPC → CPC preserves any IPC derivation
variants.construction: Compose the inclusion with a verified identity interpretation

variants.statement: No identity-on-formulas proof-preserving interpretation CPC → IPC
variants.construction: CPC excluded-middle proof contradicts Experiment 003 two-world Kripke countermodel
